As of 300 AM EST Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry conditions continue today, with increasing 
clouds ahead of an approaching storm system.

High pressure remains situated just northeast of the local area 
today, resulting in continued dry conditions. Mid and high level 
clouds will continue to filter into the area through the day as an 
upper-level trough approaches from the west and low pressure 
develops off the northern FL/southern GA coast. It will be another 
mild day for late November with high temperatures ranging from the 
mid 60s to around 70. The majority of the area should remain dry 
through the daylight hours, with rain chances beginning to increase 
from the south and southwest late tonight. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Low pressure tracking offshore will bring rain to 
much of the area Sunday into Sunday night. Specific rainfall amounts 
still remain somewhat uncertain, but some locally higher totals are 
possible.

The primary forecast challenge continues to revolve around low 
pressure developing off the FL/GA coast later today into tonight 
before tracking NE offshore. While confidence has increased in the 
overall evolution of the system, considerable uncertainty remains 
regarding placement and intensity of the associated precipitation 
shield. 

Latest 00z guidance continues to depict two distinct areas of 
precipitation, with an inland band developing ahead of the 
approaching upper-level trough and a separate area of heavier 
precipitation associated with the offshore coastal low. The 
operational ECWMF as well as the RRFS depict a fairly well 
organized inland precipitation band extending northeastward from
the Carolinas into the western half of the forecast area 
Sunday, while the GFS remains considerably drier area-wide. 
Meanwhile, the Canadian guidance remains substantially wetter, 
particularly across central VA, however this appears to be 
partly related to a different surface low evolution, which is an
outlier at this time. The 00z EPS continues to support 
measurable rainfall across much of the area, with mean QPF 
amounts averaging ~0.50" to 0.75" area-wide, locally approaching
1" in spots. It should be noted however that the mean QPF 
continues to trend drier, especially compared to the 12z Fri 
run, with a notable decrease in probabilities of QPF exceeding 
1". As a result, confidence in widespread rainfall amounts 
exceeding 1" remains relatively low, despite some of the 
deterministic guidance showing localized totals of 2" to 3"+. 

Given the continued spread among the guidance, will continue to 
favor a compromise solution with widespread rain chances Sunday, but 
maintain a more conservative QPF forecast compared to some of the 
wetter deterministic solutions. Rainfall amounts generally range 
from 0.25" to 0.75" for a majority of the area, with a locally 
higher maximum around 1" across our far western/NW locations. The 
greatest uncertainty remains with the exact placement of that 
heavier inland precipitation band, which could result in 
considerable variability in rainfall totals over a relatively short 
distance. In addition to the rain, there could still also be a brief 
period of breezy NE to NW winds along the coast on Sunday. Finally, 
given that the winds will likely be shifting and we will be coming 
out of the lower end of the astronomical high tide cycle, only minor 
tidal flooding is expected in the worst case scenario.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Drier conditions return early next week before 
another storm system potentially impacts the area around 
Thanksgiving. 

The coastal low is expected to continue tracking northeastward 
Sunday night into Monday, with rain gradually diminishing from 
SW to NE. Some rain could linger into Monday morning, especially
for eastern portions of the area. Drier conditions are then 
expected Monday into Tuesday as high pressure builds into the 
region. Attention then turns to another potential storm system 
around the Thanksgiving holiday. While considerable uncertainty 
remains regarding the exact evolution and timing of this system,
both the GFS and ECMWF continue to indicate the potential for 
another coastal low and associated precipitation across portions
of the Mid Atlantic Wednesday into Thursday. Given the holiday 
travel period, this system bears watching over the coming days. 
Confidence remains too low to determine specific rainfall 
amounts or impacts, but this system does have the potential to 
be more impactful than Sunday's storm. In addition,given the +2 
sigma high to the north, any low pressure to our south will lead
to increased NE winds and the potential for some tidal flooding
as we will be going into another King Tide cycle.
